Use advice for data set: Scope of validity: This EPD declares an average m2 JOKA INKU parquet floor 527/535 from W.&L. Jordan GmbH. JOKA INKU parquet floors 527/535 or parts thereof are produced at various production sites, all of which are owned by the manufacturer's corporate group. The vertical depth of the production processes varies and ranges from the sawmill to the packaging of the finished product. As of August 2021, JOKA INKU parquet floors 527/535 are produced in the manufacturer's own plants in Switzerland, Lithuania and Croatia. System boundary: Type of EPD: Cradle to gate with options. Modules A1–A3 and A5 Modules A1–A3 consider the production of the necessary raw materials and energy including all corresponding upstream chains as well as procurement transports. Furthermore, the entire manufacturing phase including the treatment of production waste until reaching the End-of-Waste status (EoW) is considered. Module A5 accounts for the recovery of packaging materials. Modules B2 and B5 Module B2 considers the cleaning and oiling of the parquet including the auxiliary materials required for this as well as the treatment of the resulting waste and wastewater. Module B5 declares the renovation of the parquet including the treatment of the resulting waste. Modules C1–C4 and D Module C1 describes the deconstruction. Module C2 considers the transports to the disposal processes. Module C3 includes the necessary processes for waste treatment at the end of the product life cycle. The burdens for waste treatment are represented herein until the end of waste property is reached. Resulting potentials and avoided burdens outside the system boundary are assigned to Module D. Module C4 describes the landfilling of non-recovered components of the product at the end of life. | |
Technical purpose of product or process: JOKA INKU parquet floors 527/535 are floor coverings according to EN 14342 and subsequently EN 13489, which are intended for private and commercial indoor use. They are laid either on screed or on existing other subfloors such as wood panel materials. JOKA INKU parquet floors 527/535 with tongue and groove joints are always glued to the subfloor. Products with click connection are intended for floating installation, but can also be glued down. Installation must be carried out in accordance with the installation instructions, the rules of the trade and the state of the art. The respective national regulations apply for use. | |
General comment on data set: JOKA INKU Parkettbden 527/535 sind in drei Lagen aufgebaute Holzbden mit einer Deckschichtdicke von mindestens 2,5 mm. Je nach Produktgruppe kann die Decklage aus einer einzelnen, aus einem Stck gefertigten Lamelle oder aus mehreren zusammengesetzten Einzellamellen (Schiffsbodenoptik) bestehen. Diese Decklagen werden mit einer Mittellage, bestehend aus Weichholz oder einem Holzwerkstoff und einem Gegenzug aus Weichholzfurnier mit einer Dicke von ca. 2 mm gemeinsam zu einem Produkt verpresst. Die Dimensionsbereiche der Produkte sind unter 2.3 Technische Daten, in der Tabelle "Bautechnische Daten" ersichtlich. Die Oberflchenbeschichtung erfolgt in einem mehrstufigen Prozess, in welchem schrittweise Lack- bzw. lschichten aufgetragen werden. Nach der Oberflchenbeschichtung werden die Produkte profiliert. Bei JOKA INKU Parkettbden 527/535 ist dies entweder eine Nut-und-Feder-Profilierung oder eine Klick-Verbindung, ber welche die einzelnen Parkettriemen/-dielen lngs- und querseitig miteinander verbunden werden. Die Nut-und-Feder-Profilierung setzt meist eine vollflchige Verklebung des Parkettbodens voraus. In Einzelfllen kann sie jedoch auch auf Polsterhlzern genagelt ausgefhrt werden. Die Klick-Verbindung kann sowohl schwimmend als auch verklebt verlegt werden. Die Produkte entsprechen im Allgemeinen den Anforderungen der unter 2.2 angegebenen Produktnormen. Fr das Inverkehrbringen in der Europischen Union/EFTA gilt die Verordnung (EU) Nr. 305/2011 (Bauproduktenverordnung), fr die Schweiz gilt das Bauproduktegesetz (BauPG) 933.0. Die Produkte bentigen eine Leistungserklrung unter Bercksichtigung der harmonisierten DIN EN 14342:2013-09, Holzfubden und Parkett - Eigenschaften, Bewertung der Konformitt und Kennzeichnung sowie die CE-Kennzeichnung. Als weitere produktspezifische Norm ist die EN 13489 relevant. Fr die Verwendung der Produkte gelten die jeweiligen nationalen Bestimmungen. | |
Technology description including backgro: Bauwerk Group produces its 3-layer parquet floors or parts thereof at various production sites, all of which are owned by the group. The vertical depth of the production processes varies and ranges from the sawmill to the packaging of the finished product. As of August 2021, Bauwerk Group produces the 3-layer parquet products, or parts thereof, at its plants in Switzerland, Lithuania and Croatia. At the production site in Switzerland, the 3-layer parquet products are delivered as semi-finished products from the plants in Croatia and Lithuania. Subsequently, the knotholes in the top layers are fully automatically puttied (if necessary), brushed (if desired) and subsequently subjected to surface coating before they are profiled, finally checked and packaged after several quality checks. The vertical depth of the production site in Croatia extends to the processing of roundwood in the factory's own sawmill. Subsequently, the raw wood planks are technically dried for top layer production before they are further processed into top layers at corresponding plants. The same drying and top layer production process takes place for purchased raw wood planks. The finished top layers for the 3-layer parquet production are pressed into a 3-layer semi-finished product in the Croatian factory. This means that they are pressed together with the middle layer and the counter layer in one operation and with the addition of a UF adhesive. Subsequently, any knotholes are filled, the surface of the products is coated, profiled, packed and shipped. Between and during the respective production steps, intensive quality tests are carried out, which qualify the product for the next process step. The site in Lithuania, like the Croatian site, has a sawmill that cuts round timber into raw wood planks and, after subsequent technical drying, makes the raw wood planks available for the production of top layers. From this production step onwards, the 3-layer parquet production is similar to that of the Croatian production plant. The processes in all factories are constantly controlled and documented within the framework of the factory's own production control. All data refer to the status as of August 2021.
